papers.title: Somnus, a tunable, open-source platform for automated EEG sleep scoring in physiological and disease mouse models.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Introduces Somnus, an open-source Python package for automated rodent EEG/EMG/video sleep staging, built on a base model trained across recordings from six laboratories and designed for rapid user-guided fine-tuning on uncertain epochs. It enables accurate custom sleep scorers for disease models with minimal manual correction without requiring whole-cohort hand-scoring.

papers.title: Effectiveness of Rotating Versus Fixed Three-Section Watchkeeping Schedules on Crews' Well-Being, Cognitive Performance, Sleep and Salivary Cortisol in the Navy.
papers.summary: Compared fixed versus daily rotating three-section watchkeeping schedules on board a German frigate across five underways, assessing vigilance, well-being, salivary cortisol, and sleep. Rotating schedules produced better vigilance performance, less acute cortisol disruption, and lower subjective sleepiness (especially for the 00-04 night watch), whereas fixed schedules yielded better sleep continuity.

papers.title: Associations of the Low Arousal Threshold With Arrhythmia Burden and Heart Rate Variability in Obstructive Sleep Apnea Using Polysomnography With 24-h Holter Electrocardiography.
papers.summary: Assessed whether low respiratory arousal threshold (estimated via the Edwards method) in OSA patients is associated with arrhythmia burden and heart rate variability using full-night polysomnography with 24-h Holter ECG in 166 participants. Low ArTH was associated with lower supraventricular arrhythmia burden (fewer SVPCs, SVPC pairs, and SVT episodes) and remained associated with SVPCs in multivariable analyses, though HRV differences attenuated after adjustment.

papers.title: Assessing non-invasive glymphatic MRI markers following short-term sleep loss.
papers.summary: Examined non-invasive MRI glymphatic proxies (choroid plexus volume, perivascular space volume, free water index, DTI-ALPS) across habitual sleep, sleep restriction, and sleep deprivation in a large multi-site ENIGMA-sleep dataset (n=429). Sleep deprivation was associated with decreased PVSV and ALPS and increased FWI, while sleep restriction showed the inverse pattern; indices were largely uncoupled, suggesting they reflect distinct physiological processes.

papers.title: Autonomic and Cortical Signatures of Sleepiness After Prolonged Sleep Deprivation: Pupillary Reflex, Hippus Oscillations, and Visual Evoked Potentials.
papers.summary: Tracked pupillary light reflex, hippus oscillations, visual evoked potentials, and behavioral measures across 48-hour total sleep deprivation in 24 healthy adults. Found an organized biomarker profile including early PLR timing changes, decreased late redilation diameters, sustained elevation of absolute pupillary unrest, and delayed VEP component latencies, while brief tasks and resting cardiovascular measures stayed comparatively stable.

papers.title: Divergence in sleep architecture associated with interspecific shifts in memory investment
papers.summary: Used machine-learning-facilitated video tracking of nighttime quiescence to characterize multi-state sleep in Heliconius melpomene and outgroup Dryas iulia, exploiting divergent mushroom body investment among Heliconiini butterflies. Both species showed predominantly quiet sleep but diverged in specific features, with Heliconius exhibiting more frequent active sleep bouts, suggesting that increased investment in learning and memory may relate to altered sleep architecture.

papers.title: A Benchmark of Unsupervised Circadian Phase Inference Methods for Bulk Transcriptomic Data.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Benchmarked ten unsupervised circadian phase inference methods and two clock-gene baselines across 25 datasets (16 real, 9 simulated) using aligned circular MAE and secondary rhythm-reconstruction outcomes. CHIRAL had the lowest mean MAE (1.80 h), followed by clock-gene baselines (2.15–2.20 h) and TEMPO/CYCLOPS methods (2.49–2.80 h), with accuracy dependent on dataset and clock-gene rhythm strength.

papers.title: Enhancing the Suppression of Unwanted Memories During NREM Sleep.
papers.summary: Combined the Think/No-Think paradigm with targeted memory reactivation during NREM sleep to test whether reactivating suppression instructions enhances suppression-induced forgetting. Cued suppression during sleep significantly enhanced later forgetting, accompanied by increased theta power and reduced spindle-slow oscillation up-state coupling, with reduced coupling predicting poorer later retrieval of suppressed pairs.

papers.title: Time-dependent efficacy of vitamin D3 against chronic stress-induced behavioral and circadian deficits via the hepatic VDR-clock axis.
papers.summary: Tested time-dependent vitamin D3 administration in a mouse chronic unpredictable mild stress model, giving VitD3 in the morning versus evening. Evening administration more effectively improved anxiety- and depression-like behaviors, hippocampal integrity, TNF-α, sleep duration, and serotonin synthesis, and more effectively restored hepatic Vdr rhythmic oscillation, with C. elegans validation supporting a VDR-circadian clock axis.

papers.title: Changes and trajectories in sleep duration and risk of premature all-cause and cardiovascular disease mortality.
papers.summary: In a population-based cohort of 13,621 Chinese adults, relative increases in sleep duration of ≥30% were associated with higher risks of premature all-cause mortality (HR 1.78) and cardiovascular mortality (HR 2.20) compared to stable sleep duration, and trajectories toward long sleep (>9 h/day) were linked to increased premature CVD mortality.

papers.title: Circadian phase alignment promotes survival under predictive oxidative stress.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Used Synechococcus elongatus strains with altered free-running period to decouple circadian period from phase angle of entrainment across seasonal photoperiods. Strains whose stress-response programs peaked with the stressor outcompeted early- or late-peaking counterparts, and the wild-type period was uniquely plastic in aligning stress responses across all photoperiods.

papers.title: Altered EEG-derived co-fluctuation structure in disorders of consciousness.
papers.summary: Adapted a co-fluctuation framework to resting-state EEG to characterize dynamic functional connectivity across varying conscious states, comparing high- and low-amplitude frames against null models. Loss of consciousness was associated with reduced stability of co-fluctuations and a shift toward random system dynamics, and combined high-/low-amplitude frame parameters showed diagnostic potential for distinguishing disorders of consciousness states.

papers.title: Circadian Clock Coordination of the Notch-to-Wnt Signaling Switch Promotes Regenerative Myogenesis
papers.summary: Using genetic and pharmacological approaches, this study identifies the circadian clock as a regulator of the Notch-to-Wnt signaling switch that promotes muscle stem cell expansion and myogenic differentiation during regeneration; clock activation enhanced regenerative myogenesis in dystrophic mouse and human myoblasts.

papers.title: The use of wearable devices in the community to detect symptom severity and relapse of psychosis: A systematic review.
papers.journal: The Australian and New Zealand journal of psychiatry
papers.summary: This systematic review of 18 unique studies found that wearable devices measuring actigraphy, sleep-wake cycles, and heart rate are feasible for monitoring psychotic symptom severity and may detect relapse in community-dwelling people with psychosis, though most studies were short-term and had serious risk of bias.

papers.title: Advanced Two-Stage Authentication with EEG: Inter-Subject P300 ERP Classification Using EEGNet for User Recognition.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: The study developed a two-stage EEG-based authentication framework using P300 event-related potentials and the EEGNet convolutional neural network, achieving up to 95% precision and a mean accuracy of 96.10% for both identification and authentication across 16 participants and three sessions.

papers.title: Clocks In Sync: A mixed methods pilot feasibility trial of blue-light blocking therapy and time-restricted eating, alone or in combination for mania in bipolar disorder.
authors: Clocks In Sync Investigators and Coordinators
papers.summary: In a mixed-methods pilot randomized trial with 21 inpatients with bipolar mania, blue-blocking glasses and/or time-restricted eating were feasible with 80% adherence; greater improvements in Young Mania Rating Scale scores were observed in groups receiving blue-blocking glasses compared to time-restricted eating alone.

papers.title: Rheumatoid Arthritis and Sleep Disturbances: A Narrative Review of Bidirectional Mechanisms.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes clinical and mechanistic evidence for a bidirectional relationship between rheumatoid arthritis and sleep disturbances, implicating peripheral-to-central inflammatory signaling, circadian disruption, HPA-axis dysfunction, autonomic hyperarousal, and central sensitization. The authors note that most evidence is cross-sectional or from small treatment studies, so causality remains uncertain, and recommend distinguishing specific sleep disorders from nonspecific symptoms and combining RA management with disorder-specific sleep treatment.

papers.title: Feasibility of Vibrotactile P50 Sensory-Gating Assessment Using Portable EEG
papers.summary: This study tested the feasibility of assessing P50 sensory gating with portable 32-channel EEG using vibrotactile paired stimuli in 15 healthy adults, comparing responses with an auditory condition. Vibrotactile stimulation elicited time-locked P50 suppression (mean S2/S1 ratio 0.524) that did not differ significantly from the auditory condition (0.521; paired difference 0.0029, p = 0.807).

papers.title: Clinical features of the postictal state in adults with epilepsy: A cross-sectional survey.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional survey of 298 adults with epilepsy characterized the frequency, duration, and severity of 14 postictal symptoms, finding that 95% experienced at least one, most commonly fatigue/sleepiness (84%), confusion (75%), and memory problems (69%). Mean postictal symptom burden correlated with quality of life and epilepsy-related disability, and sleep/rest, medication, and food/drinks were the most common alleviating factors.

papers.title: Lifestyle-Based Interventions for Major Depressive Disorder and Their Role Alongside Antidepressant Treatment: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 34 reports from 29 randomized trials evaluated lifestyle-based interventions delivered alongside antidepressant treatment in adults with major depressive disorder. Structured exercise showed the most consistent favorable signal, sleep/circadian and bright-light interventions showed possible but inconsistent short-term benefits, and overall certainty of evidence was low to very low, with no eligible trial of whole-diet intervention alone.

papers.title: Accelerometry-Derived REM Sleep Behavior Disorder Score Is Associated with Incident Parkinson's Disease in the UK Biobank
papers.summary: Applying a validated machine learning RBD classifier to 7-day wrist accelerometry in 87,975 UK Biobank participants followed for 10 years, the highest RBD-risk stratum (>99th percentile) showed an approximately fivefold increased hazard of incident Parkinson's disease with a dose-dependent relationship. The association was independent of PD polygenic risk score and synergistic with genetic risk, with high specificity (99.2%) supporting accelerometry for prodromal PD risk enrichment.

papers.title: Real-time wearable detection of respiratory infections in pediatric transplant households.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: In a Phase IV trial cohort of 146 pediatric solid organ transplant recipients and household members, a resting heart rate-based real-time alerting algorithm was applied to detect respiratory virus infection, with 29 of 31 antigen-test outcomes (93.5%) corresponding to influenza, COVID, or other patient-reported symptoms. The authors describe heart rate, activity, and sleep/circadian features around alarm events as candidate features for algorithm improvement.

papers.title: Evidence of high rates of burnout symptoms in a cohort with cluster headache.
papers.summary: In a Swedish cohort of 373 cluster headache patients, 65.9% of those in active bout had high burnout scores (>3.75 on Shirom-Melamed Burnout Questionnaire) versus 37.5% in remission (OR=3.22, 95% CI 1.93-5.38). High burnout was also associated with female sex and sleep deprivation as an attack trigger, and scores decreased with longer remission duration.

papers.title: Comparison of quality of life between docetaxel and weekly paclitaxel in the neoadjuvant or adjuvant treatment of breast cancer.
papers.summary: In an observational cohort of 82 stage II-III breast cancer patients receiving adjuvant/neoadjuvant taxanes, docetaxel (every 3 weeks) was associated with higher depressive symptoms and lower life satisfaction at peak treatment burden compared to weekly paclitaxel, while global quality-of-life and sleep quality were comparable. Hematologic adverse events were more frequent with docetaxel and peripheral neuropathy with weekly paclitaxel.

papers.title: Heterogeneous perceived stress profiles and static-dynamic symptom networks of PTSD, anxiety, depression, and insomnia in firefighters: An integrated latent profile and network analysis.
papers.summary: Latent profile analysis of 8428 Chinese firefighters identified three perceived stress profiles (task-related thinking, consistent, imbalanced), with the imbalanced profile reporting highest stress and the consistent profile greatest psychopathological burden. Cross-sectional and longitudinal networks revealed profile-specific symptom connectivity, with sleep disturbance and low sleep satisfaction consistently influential.

papers.title: Longitudinal Pain Profiles and Their Clinical and Genetic Correlates in 624,996 U.S. Veterans.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: In a Million Veteran Program cohort of 624,996 participants and 51.7 million outpatient pain ratings, Gaussian finite mixture modeling identified three longitudinal pain profiles: stable no pain, stable mild pain, and mild-to-moderate increasing pain. The increasing pain profile had markedly higher odds of chronic pain, opioid use disorder, opioid exposure, depression, and PTSD, and polygenic scores for depression, insomnia, ADHD, and tobacco use disorder were the most consistent predictors of increasing pain.

papers.title: Risk of obstructive sleep apnea in patients with polycystic ovary syndrome by body mass index: Retrospective cohort study with Korean nationwide population-based cohort.
papers.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
papers.summary: In a Korean nationwide retrospective cohort of 33,638 PCOS patients and 98,110 controls, PCOS was associated with increased risk of obstructive sleep apnea (HR 1.483, 95% CI 1.029-2.137), and obesity at PCOS diagnosis further elevated risk (BMI HR 1.104 per unit). The findings support OSA screening in PCOS, especially with obesity.

papers.title: The Relationship of Triglyceride/Glucose Index with Disease Severity, Sleep, and Cognitive Functions in Patients with Geriatric Depression: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study with Healthy Controls.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 76 drug-naïve older adults with major depression and 40 controls, the triglyceride/glucose index (TyG) was significantly higher in depressed patients and independently associated with depression status (adjusted OR ~24.9), correlating with depression severity but not with cognitive function or insomnia severity. A TyG cutoff >8.78 showed 63.16% sensitivity and 95.00% specificity for depression.

papers.title: Perioperative non-invasive brain stimulation for the prevention of postoperative delirium: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of nine randomized controlled trials (1451 participants) found that perioperative non-invasive brain stimulation was associated with lower postoperative delirium risk (RR 0.41, 95% CI 0.31-0.56; moderate-certainty evidence), without reduced hospital stay; the authors conclude the evidence does not establish a class effect or support routine use.

papers.title: Differential expression of circadian clock genes and proteins in gingival tissues from patients with stage III grade B periodontitis: a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: In gingival biopsies from 60 systemically healthy, non-smoking participants, compared stage III grade B periodontitis samples to health and gingivitis showed higher CLOCK and Per3 and lower CRY1, CRY2, and Rev-Erb-β at gene and protein levels, with lower Per2 protein in both diseased groups. RANKL was higher and OPG lower in periodontitis, and clock gene expression correlated with clinical periodontal parameters; single-time-point sampling was interpreted as differential expression.

papers.title: Women with the FMR1 premutation: a within-family observational sibling study.
papers.journal: BMJ connections. Clinical genetics and genomics
papers.summary: A within-family observational sibling study of 67 women from 30 families used multilevel modeling to compare FMR1 premutation carriers with their biological sisters. It found the premutation effect stronger than the effect of parenting a child with fragile X syndrome, with many adverse differences emerging when mothers with the premutation and a child with FXS were compared with sisters with normal-range CGG repeats.

papers.title: Orforglipron for Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Results From 2 Randomized Clinical Trials (ATTAIN-OSA).
papers.summary: Two 52-week phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials (ATTAIN-OSA) in adults with moderate to severe OSA and obesity or overweight found orforglipron reduced apnea-hypopnea index vs placebo by 13.2 events/h in trial 1 and 12.0 events/h in trial 2. Six of seven key secondary end points favored orforglipron; gastrointestinal events were more frequent with drug.

papers.title: Cognitive disengagement syndrome and alexisomia: examining the moderating role of anxiety-depression symptoms, stress, and insomnia symptoms among a sample of Lebanese adults.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 877 Lebanese adults, higher cognitive disengagement syndrome (CDS) traits were significantly associated with greater alexisomia; anxiety-depression and insomnia symptoms significantly moderated this association, attenuating it at higher symptom levels, whereas stress did not.

papers.title: Health Information Literacy Moderates the Associations of Perceived Social Support with Insomnia and Infertility Psychological Distress in Women Undergoing Assisted Reproductive Technology: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.summary: A cross-sectional survey of 1007 women undergoing assisted reproductive technology found perceived social support negatively associated with infertility psychological distress, with a significant indirect association through insomnia; health information literacy moderated the associations among social support, insomnia, and distress. These findings suggest psychosocial assessment should jointly consider social support, sleep problems, and health information literacy.

papers.title: Avermectin poisoning with panic-like symptoms: a case series.
papers.summary: A case series of two men with avermectin poisoning reports toxic effects including respiratory failure, hypotension, acidosis, coma, and delirium after oral ingestion, and local swelling with panic-like symptoms after intramuscular injection. In the oral case, panic-like symptoms were identified on psychiatric evaluation and improved with specialized treatment.

papers.title: A Local Enrichment Computational Framework to Identify Disease-Enriched Physical Activity Patterns
papers.summary: The authors introduce LocPA, a computational framework using confounder-adjusted activity profiling, similarity networks, and local disease-enrichment testing, and apply it to UK Biobank accelerometry to identify low-activity and sleep-disrupted physical activity phenotypes enriched across six diseases, with replication in NHANES.

papers.title: Transient HBV entry into cerebrospinal fluid following blood-brain barrier disruption: a case of HSV-2 encephalitis with polymicrobial detection elucidated by serial targeted next-generation sequencing.
papers.summary: A case report of HSV-2 encephalitis in a 42-year-old man with untreated hepatitis B, in which serial targeted next-generation sequencing of cerebrospinal fluid detected HSV-2, HHV-4, and HBV; synchronous viral clearance after acyclovir/tenofovir therapy and BBB restoration indicated transient passive HBV entry during barrier disruption rather than CNS infection.

papers.title: Gut microbiome depletion aggravates glial-mediated Alzheimer's disease pathology through inflammatory, metabolic, and proteostatic dysregulation.
papers.summary: Using humanized Drosophila Alzheimer's disease models with glial transgene expression, this study found that antibiotic-induced gut microbiome depletion increased inflammatory signaling, impaired autophagy, lipid dysregulation, and accumulation of Aβ42 and phospho-tau, worsening sleep-circadian disruption and learning/memory deficits. The results identify the gut microbiome as a regulator of glial homeostasis and AD pathology via inflammatory, metabolic, and proteostatic pathways.

papers.title: URBANOME: an exposome-based framework linking urban interventions to molecular, health, and policy-relevant outcomes.
papers.summary: Presents the URBANOME exposome-based framework for evaluating co-created urban interventions (active mobility, greening, traffic calming) across nine European cities using personal exposure monitoring, health measures, multi-omics, and cost-benefit analysis; pilot before-after findings included reduced air-pollution annoyance and sleep-related breathing problems, attenuated pollution-related FVC differences, and a preliminary four-metabolite pre/post panel (small sample, unvalidated).

papers.title: Cross-species multi-omics integration reveals lung alterations in acute kidney injury across mouse, pig, and human airway organoid models.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Integrating clinical Epic Cosmos data with cross-species RNA-seq and proteomics from pig, mouse, and human airway organoid models, this study characterized acute kidney injury-associated lung alterations, showing higher mortality in the AKI-lung subgroup and a temporal shift from hyper-acute post-translational microvascular breakdown to transcriptional inflammatory and ER stress responses. Primary human donor lungs confirmed selective downregulation of CLOCK transcript in AKI.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
